description: Write a pandas ETL script for telecom_co that maintains a Type 2 slowly changing customer dimension. Inputs are the existing dimension and a daily snapshot of customers with an effective date (2025-03-10 in the sample). The script should: (1) compare each incoming customer to its current dimension row on the tracked attributes (tier, region), (2) for changed customers close the current row (valid_to = effective date, is_current = false) and insert a new current row (valid_from = effective date, valid_to = null), (3) insert new customers, (4) leave unchanged customers untouched, (5) never create more than one current row per customer. In the sample, rows are tagged with _dataset to distinguish the existing dimension from the incoming snapshot.
edge_cases: c3 has region null on both sides: null == null must count as 'unchanged' (NaN != NaN in pandas would create a spurious new version)
Validity ranges are half-open [valid_from, valid_to): the closed row ends on the same date the new row starts
Running the script twice for the same snapshot_date must not create additional versions
The comparison must be made against the current row only (is_current = true), not against every historical row
A customer absent from the snapshot is left as is (no implicit delete)
common_failure_modes: FM1: Joining the snapshot to all dimension rows instead of current rows creates duplicate versions
FM7: Null-unsafe comparison generates a new version every day for customers with null attributes
FM2: Closing rows with valid_to = effective date - 1 leaves a one-day gap for timestamp-based lookups
